reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only confirms that the parent Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a BCS-type superconductor in the dirty limit, but provides no data on annealing, ordering, defect density, or their effects on scattering, mean free path, or Tc. The key mechanistic premises linking annealing to enhanced superconductivity are entirely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Annealing reduces defect-induced electron scattering in the alloy.
Reduced scattering increases electron mean free path.
Increased mean free path strengthens electron–phonon coupling in the dirty limit.
Stronger coupling sharpens the superconducting transition and raises Tc.
The alloy is a dirty-limit BCS superconductor where disorder suppresses superconductivity.
